sources.title: Why a changed solver needs policy revalidation
sources.details: A frozen selection rule was accepted under measured conditions for theta_old (solver weights), e (effort) and d (device/decoding). Its premise is a relation R(theta_old,e,d) between success and cost. Replacing theta_old by theta_new does not establish R(theta_new,e,d), so acceptance must be checked for the new tuple. This is an implication-boundary argument, not an assertion that every weight update worsens results or changes runtime. A direct CPU linear example with unchanged architecture and input 2 gives outputs 2 and -2 after loading weights 1 and -1, establishing that unchanged names/config alone do not force unchanged behavior.
